name: Mossaby Parish
region: Southern Småland, in the forest uplands
description: Mossaby is a poor forest parish in the Småland uplands, a scattering of small farms and crofts on stony ground between spruce forest, bogs and lakes. The fields are made by carrying stones off them for generations, piled in long walls through the woods. Since the famine years at the end of the 1860s, families have been leaving for America almost every month, and empty cottages stand with their doors nailed shut.
seasonNotes: October. The rowans are red with berries and the birches yellow against dark spruce, but the stony fields have given a thin harvest again. Mists lie over the bogs each morning and rise slowly through the trees. Potatoes are being dug and stored, and lingonberries picked in the forest. The rains come and the stream rises enough for the mill to grind. The days grow short and cold, and the first frost blackens the potato tops.
travel: From Uppsala by rail via Stockholm and the southern main line to Nässjö, about twelve hours, then by coach or farm cart into the forest, most of a day on poor roads.
publicFacts: In the famine years of 1867 and 1868 the harvest failed twice and the parish went hungry; many sold their land.
Some forty people have left Mossaby for America in the last three years, most for Minnesota and Illinois; their letters and tickets arrive by post.
An emigration agent visits the parish twice a year selling passages via Gothenburg and Liverpool.
The vicar holds the household examination in each village in November and keeps careful records of who has gone.
The parish is crossed by stone walls built by generations of farmers clearing their fields.
A miller grinds at the stream mill only in autumn and spring, when there is enough water.
The revival preachers have a strong following in the parish, and many families hold devotions at home.
The wise man in the forest is visited by people from three parishes for sick animals and lost things.

places.name: Mossaby Church
places.description: The church is a small white building with a tarred wooden tower, standing on a hill of glacial gravel above the lake. The churchyard wall is built of the same grey stones as every field wall in the parish. Yellow birch leaves blow across the graves. Inside it smells of damp, and the plaster on the walls is cracked.

affordances.name: Sacristy
affordances.description: A small vaulted room off the chancel where the vicar robes.

contains.name: Vestment cupboard
contains.description: A tall cupboard of chasubles, the surplice and spare altar candles.

contains.name: Parish chest
contains.description: An ancient iron-banded chest with three locks for the communion silver and old deeds.

affordances.name: Bell tower
affordances.description: Steep ladders up to the bells, bird droppings on the beams, wind through the louvres.

affordances.name: Church loft
affordances.description: The dusty space above the vaults, full of broken pews and old hatchments.

places.name: Mossaby Parsonage
places.ownerRole: the vicar of the parish, who lives here and serves the church
places.description: The parsonage is a plain red house with white corners, the best building in the parish though its roof leaks. Lingonberries are spread on cloths in the kitchen. The vicar works by lamplight early in the afternoon, adding notes of 'moved to North America' to the registers. The glebe fields around it are as stony as everyone else's.

places.name: Ingeborgs gård
places.ownerRole: a freeholder farming family; the farm is named for a great-grandmother, Ingeborg
places.description: A small farm on a slope above the lake, its grey timber house surrounded by birches and stone walls. The farmer and his sons are digging potatoes in the wet field. Smoke rises from the bathhouse where malt is drying. A pig is fattening in a pen for the slaughter.

places.name: Stenbacken
places.ownerRole: a crofter family preparing to leave for America
places.description: A tiny croft on a stony hill among the spruces, with a grey cottage and a byre for one cow. The family is preparing to leave for America in the spring, and the chest is already packed in the corner. Mist drips from the trees. The potato patch has been dug and only stones remain.

places.name: Rävmossen
places.ownerRole: a crofter family on the bog
places.description: The cottage stands at the edge of a wide bog, its windows dark, its door nailed shut since the family left for America last year. Nobody has bought it, and the meadow is going back to heather and birch scrub. The mist rolls in from the bog in the morning. A path of logs leads across the bog to the forest beyond.

places.name: Bäckakvarn
places.description: A small grey mill stands where the stream falls through a rocky gorge in the forest, its wheel turning now that the autumn rains have come. The water foams white over the stones and the noise fills the narrow valley. Moss and ferns cover every surface. The miller is an old man who grinds for half the parish in the few weeks the water lasts.

affordances.description: The pond behind the dam, black and still, with a sluice gate.

places.name: The Wise Man's Cottage
places.ownerRole: the wise man, a cunning man the parish both fears and needs
places.description: Deep in the forest, an hour's walk from any farm, a small cottage stands by a spring among old spruces. Bundles of plants and bark hang from every beam. A cat watches from the window. People come here from far away, though they rarely speak of it.

affordances.name: Cottage room

places.name: The Parish Smithy
places.description: The smithy stands at the crossroads in the middle of the parish, an old building of stone and timber. The smith makes scythes and axes for the forest farms and repairs the emigrants' trunks. The forge glows red in the grey autumn afternoon. Farmers stop there to talk and exchange news from America.
